Still watching for the satire remark and missed concert to come back. Pay is huge and grows fast. Choices seem to have real consequences.

best_moment.what: The Background Check, where I disclosed everything including the dormant company and it turned my liabilities into proof of good judgement. Honesty paid off in a way I didn't expect.

worst_moment.what: The Budget Round. I bid big against a flat envelope, but I didn't know what any of it meant, so it was just a choice between two bits of jargon.

skip_year.why: Telling an adviser I'd thought about politics was a quiet, low-drama beat and mostly set up later years. Nothing happened in it.

answer.held_back_by: I lost the single seat by under two points, and the card said it was never about me, so apparently it was the party or the ward. I gambled on the solo seat instead of the GRC team, so that choice probably cost me. I never saw the satire remark or the missed concert come back, so it wasn't my integrity or those choices.
answer.ending_fair_why: I shook every hand and still lost by under two points, and the game says it was never about me. After nine years of choices that felt weighty, I couldn't tell which one decided it. The single-seat gamble might have, but the game never showed me. It felt like a coin flip dressed up as a consequence.
answer.chase_next: I'd go for the GRC team route and try to win the election and become a minister, since the title promises ministerial pay and I never got there. I'd also like to see whether the satire remark and the missed concert ever come back.
answer.play_again_why: The ending annoyed me enough that I want to test the GRC choice. The run was short, and I want to see if the callbacks I was waiting for actually exist.

answer.title_fit_why: The pay was huge and grew fast, and it was the thing I noticed most each year. The other title sounds like a civil service term I'd have to look up, and I never learned what it meant here.
